summary:
Welcome to the Orbit Space Program! For the NASA Space Mission design game, we didn’t just build a game; we built a solar system explorer powered by NASA data. Step into the program and choose your destination among the various planets in our solar system. Build your space-exploring vessels through engineering decisions guided by NASA data.

Your goal is to equip your spaceship with the right instruments and equipment to help you succeed in your space-exploring missions. Through this game, the bridge between planning and implementing space mission design is effectively crossed. This aspect is important because users can see how much resource constraints can impact the outcome of the mission.
details:
Our Project’s Purpose

Orbit Space Program is an interactive educational game that allows users to explore the solar system by completing unique space missions. Players select a planet they want to visit and learn about, design and build a rocket using realistic parts, and manage their budget while considering the requirements of their destination.

The players make informed decisions about the selection of their rocket parts based on NASA data. However, upon mission failures, players face financial troubles, forcing them to make smart choices about the selection of their parts. Once their rocket is built, they take it through a flight simulation to reach their selected planet. Upon successful completion of the mission, players earn credit and unlock information and facts about the planet they visited, helping them discover more about our solar system.

Benefits of Our Project

Our project makes learning about space exploration more enjoyable and interactive. It teaches users that space missions are more than just building rockets. Players must consider factors including capital, rocket performance, destination requirements, and the purpose of space missions. Users gain scientific knowledge by discovering facts about each planet after completing their mission. This helps develop problem-solving, critical-thinking, and decision-making skills while making learning entertaining.

Impact of Our Project

The intended impact of Orbit Space Program is for individuals with intellectual curiosity or interest in aerospace engineering to get hands-on experience in the industry. Many don't know the challenges involved in completing space missions, and they struggle to transition from textbook math to real-world mission planning. Existing simulations of missions are too complex or expensive for everyday classrooms.

We want users to recognize that every mission requires planning, engineering, resource management, and decision-making, while keeping it easy to understand.Through interactive gameplay, users can experience some of the challenges of designing and launching a rocket using real NASA data. 

Such challenges include: calculating thrust-to-weight ratios, selecting science instruments to meet specific mission objectives, rocket-design trade-offs, fuel efficiency, balancing costs, and balancing rocket performance with resource constraints. Our game equips students with a practical understanding of the difficulty of space missions, while allowing them to deepen their curiosity in space exploration through simple games. 

Tools Used

The tools and technologies we used to develop our project include:

  • VS Code: Used to write, edit, and organize our code.
  • GitHub: Used to manage our code and collaborate as a team.
  • Pixilart: Used to create pixel art and visual elements for our game.
  • Perplexity: Used to research information and gather ideas.
  • Codex: Used to assist with coding and development.
  • JavaScript, HTML, and CSS: The programming languages used to develop our game.
  • Hardware and operating systems: We used our personal laptops, working across Windows and macOS

Creativity of Our Project

Our project is creative since it combines space missions, planning a mission, rocket design, financing, and learning in one interactive game. Instead of simply presenting users with information about planets, we allow users to experience what it is like to plan and complete a space mission. Each mission has a unique challenge, so users need to make certain decisions concerning rocket elements, budget, and capabilities. The flight simulation and information about the planets are unlocked at the end of each mission, emphasizing the educational value of the project.
